# Capture corpus for the policy replay gate. One fixture per line.
# Build with: uv run mktrace.py <NvFBCR.log> <name>.trace "<description>"
# (mktrace.py lives in this directory; run the suite afterwards for the bounds)
kcd_60x2_mapcycles.trace
kcd_60x2_mapcycles_postfix.trace
# Steady walking, the regime the map-cycle fixtures do not cover: they are dominated by
# stall recovery, so a selection change that quietly raised gameplay synth would pass them.
kcd_60x2_walk.trace
# Same content and flip rate as the walk above, but a scanout grid that jitters 5.5x more
# (step IQR 1610us vs 291us) for reasons still unexplained. Kept because the jitter broke a
# fixed anchor bound that the clean walk passed: a rule tuned on one grid is not a rule.
kcd_60x2_walk_jitter.trace
# Varied content WITH flip data (the walks are steady; the map cycles carry no flips): the
# fixture that exercises stage-6 delivery-lateness correction against real late events.
kcd_60x2_join_events.trace
# The regimes the x2 corpus cannot gate. An x2 assumption that fails silently-inert (or
# silently-wrong) elsewhere must break one of these instead: x3 rotates the batch
# composition through the source period; FG-off is 1-member batches on a metronome grid.
kcd_60x3_walk.trace
kcd_60x1_fgoff.trace
# The live -dejit validation run: the only fixture carrying a proven blend REMOVAL (a
# 5032us late delivery costing an isolated mid-gameplay blend). Every other fixture proves
# the correction does no harm; this one proves it does its job.
kcd_60x2_dejit_event.trace
# 69 minutes of real streamed gameplay, desktop trimmed off both ends. Every other fixture
# is minutes of map cycles or walking at 8-9% synth; this one is an hour of the content the
# relay actually ships, at 0.6%, where blends are ISOLATED events rather than transition
# bursts. It is the only fixture long enough to measure the isolated-blend rate at all
# (75 removals, 73 of them single-frame events), and the only one carrying the once-per-
# second NvFBC delivery hitch that produces half of them.
gm_60x2_gameplay_hour.trace
# THE D3D11 FLIP PRESENT, on Avatar. Everything above is the D3D9 vsync path, where a
# frame-generated source runs the compose clock at the DISPLAYED rate: two presents per source
# frame, the comb lock structurally unable to engage, half the decisions landing between teeth.
# These present on the SINK's own clock at 1:1, so the lock holds engaged and the steady state
# is pure passthrough. A policy change that assumes the old two-presents-per-tooth geometry
# passes every fixture above and fails here.
#
# Each configuration ships TWO fixtures, because one window cannot gate both regimes. The
# _steady pair is a single benchmark test with no fade at either end, where the field decided
# passthrough on EVERY present: any spurious blend fails it immediately, and the replay model
# tracks it almost exactly. The _bench pair is all nine tests across three bench runs with
# every inter-test fade kept, which is where the source drops to 60 Hz on a fade to black and
# the relay blends across the hole. The model tracks a fade about half as well as it tracks
# gameplay, so the _bench bounds are looser by construction and gate what the model can see;
# that is why the _steady fixtures exist beside them rather than instead of them.
avatar_60x2_flip_steady.trace
avatar_60x2_flip_bench.trace
# The same configuration with generated-frame substitution armed (-subgen, which implies the
# driver change map). What it pins is a NEGATIVE: substitution fires 38 times in six minutes
# and changes nothing. The cause was originally read as the tooth guard having already removed
# the mid-tooth blends; measuring the change map on this log says otherwise. 99.5% of batches
# report ZERO changed blocks between the real member and the generated member paired with it,
# so the ring refuses the retracted slot as a duplicate and the policy never sees a candidate.
# The 59x2 subgen pair further down shows the identical 99.6% at a ratio where the tooth guard
# is not even armed, which is what separates the two explanations.
# A change that makes -subgen active again at x2 breaks this pair and nothing else.
avatar_60x2_subgen_steady.trace
avatar_60x2_subgen_bench.trace
# Frame generation OFF: arrivals, presents and source flips all 1:1:1, so keep-real has nothing
# to collapse and every present has exactly one candidate frame. The FG-off fixture further up
# covers 1-member batches on the D3D9 path, where the present clock is DWM's; these cover them
# where the present is the sink's own. The degenerate geometry - no pairing, no collapse, no
# side to choose - so anything that only works because a batch has two members, or because the
# target can sit between teeth, has nowhere to hide.
avatar_60x1_flip_steady.trace
avatar_60x1_flip_bench.trace
# The non-integer ratio. 59 fps into a 60 Hz sink: no comb can hold it, so the bracket phase
# ramps through a full source period once per second and the compositor synthesizes whenever
# the target sits more than a quarter period from a real frame - about half of every beat, and
# 44% of all presents. Every other fixture here runs the blend path at 0-9%; these run it at
# maximum duty, with weights piled in the 0.25-0.75 midrange rather than at the edges. The
# passthrough threshold, the stickiness band and the tooth guard all decide something on nearly
# every present, so a change to any of them shows up here first.
avatar_59x1_flip_steady.trace
avatar_59x1_flip_bench.trace
# The SAME 59 fps source and the same content, declared as -src 60. Nobody types -src 59; the
# flag will always name a nominal target rate, so a source that misses it by a frame is the
# realistic configuration and this pair is what it costs. Every derived period comes out 1.7%
# short - lag 95833 vs 96186 us, passthrough threshold 4166 vs 4237, comb 16666 vs 16949 - and
# the output is indistinguishable: 44.8% synth against 44.3%, blend runs of median 26 against
# 25. What DOES move is the comb: an exact 1.000 ratio makes M=1 a true match rather than a
# 1.67%-error one, the gate engages twice as often and holds half as long, and the pull tail
# halves. Paired with avatar_59x1_flip_* this isolates -src as a single variable.
avatar_59at60_flip_steady.trace
avatar_59at60_flip_bench.trace
# 59 base with frame generation x2, declared -src 60. The pair that proves keep-real erases the
# frame generator: arrivals come at 115/s in pairs, keep-real collapses each to its real member
# at 59.04/s, and the policy then walks the identical 59:60 ramp the FG-off pair walks - 45.1%
# synth against 44.8%, blend runs of the same length, the comb lock never engaging once. Same
# beat, twice the arrival traffic. It also carries the only VRR source in the corpus: the panel
# is G-SYNC and the individual flips wander 7.1 to 9.9 ms even while the per-second count holds
# 118, so a policy that quietly assumes an evenly spaced source grid fails here and nowhere else.
avatar_59x2_flip_steady.trace
avatar_59x2_flip_bench.trace
# The same 59x2 configuration with -subgen armed. What it pins is WHY substitution is inert,
# which is not what the 60x2 subgen pair above was originally read to say. The blocker is not
# the tooth guard and not the policy gate: it is the ring's duplicate refusal. The driver's
# change map reports ZERO changed blocks between the real member and the generated member it
# was paired with on 99.6% of batches, so the retracted slot is never marked generated, the
# policy never sees a candidate, and 24 substitutions happen in six minutes against 8300
# blends. Synth share is 45.1%, identical to the no-subgen pair. If a capture-path change ever
# makes generated frames genuinely reachable, this fixture moves and nothing else does.
avatar_59x2_subgen_steady.trace
avatar_59x2_subgen_bench.trace
